chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who comes to me seeking food and sale [of goods] from me, and I do not have [the goods] with me; is it permissible for me to sell it to him, fix its price, then buy it from another place and deliver it to him? He said: 'There is no harm if the price is fixed.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell goods you do not currently possess in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* validates the *bay' al-madmun* (guaranteed sale) mechanism, where a seller commits to providing specific goods by fixing the price and subsequently procuring them, a practice widely used in Shia commercial jurisprudence to facilitate trade without immediate possession. It clarifies that the validity of the contract hinges on the certainty of the price (*si'r*) at the time of agreement, ensuring transparency even when the item is not yet in hand. This ruling supports the flexibility of Islamic contracts in allowing deferred delivery as long as the essential elements of the sale are clearly defined and guaranteed.
